description: Port of Clippy 0.1.99's allow_attributes_without_reason: reports every #[allow(..)] and #[expect(..)] attribute, inner or outer, one a #[cfg_attr(..)] expands to included (at the expanded attribute), whose last item is not `reason = ".."`. The lint needs Rust 1.81 (lint reasons, `suppress.clippy.msrv`). What a macro invocation's or macro_rules! body's token tree holds, and whether a #[cfg] predicate holds in a build, are not read. A #[cfg_attr] is read as active unless its first argument is exactly `test`, `any()` or `not(clippy)`, the predicates the suppression engine reads as off whatever the build; every other predicate is read as active. Each allow or expect a #[cfg_attr] expands to is checked on its own for a last `reason = ".."` item and reported at its own span (`allow(..)`, as Clippy reports the expanded attribute); a list nested deeper than two parentheses inside it is not read.

violation.message: Add a reason to this attribute, e.g. #[allow(dead_code, reason = "why")], saying why the lint is silenced.
Add a reason to this cfg_attr's allow or expect, e.g. allow(dead_code, reason = "why"), saying why the lint is silenced.
